items.prompt: Which word is the subordinating conjunction? We stayed inside because it was raining.

options.why: Stayed is a verb.
Inside tells us where.
Raining is a verb.

hints: A conjunction joins two clauses.
Find the word that starts the second part of the sentence.
Split the sentence into two parts. Which word links them?
items.explanation: Because joins the main clause we stayed inside to the subordinate clause it was raining. It gives a reason.

items.prompt: Choose the best conjunction. ___ it was very hot, Lina wore her jacket.

options.why: Because would mean the heat made her wear a jacket, which does not make sense.
Unless means except if, which does not make sense here.
So shows a result. It does not fit at the start of this sentence.

hints: Wearing a jacket on a hot day is surprising.
Look for the conjunction that shows a contrast, when one thing is surprising after another.
Try each word in the gap and read the sentence aloud.
items.explanation: Although shows a contrast. It was hot, which makes wearing a jacket surprising.

items.prompt: Match each main clause to the subordinate clause that completes it.
hints: Each pair must make sense as one sentence.
Think about what each conjunction does: if is a condition, until is time, because is a reason.
Start with You will not get wet. What would keep you dry?
items.explanation: Each subordinate clause adds a condition, a time or a reason to the main clause, and the whole sentence makes sense.

items.prompt: Sort the clauses into main clauses and subordinate clauses.
hints: A main clause makes sense on its own.
A subordinate clause starts with a word such as while, because or although, and it does not make sense alone.
Read each clause on its own. Does it sound complete?
items.explanation: The cat slept, we walked home and Dewi finished her painting make sense alone. The others begin with conjunctions and need a main clause.

items.prompt: Which sentence is a complex sentence?

options.text: The sun set and the bats flew out.
options.why: This joins two main clauses with and, so it is a compound sentence.

options.text: When the sun set, the bats flew out of the cave.
The bats flew out of the cave.
options.why: This is a simple sentence with one clause.
This is a simple sentence.

hints: A complex sentence has a main clause and at least one subordinate clause.
Look for a conjunction such as when, because or although.
Find the sentence that has a part which could not stand on its own.
items.explanation: When the sun set is a subordinate clause and the bats flew out of the cave is the main clause, so it is a complex sentence.

items.prompt: Write one conjunction to fill the gap. You cannot go swimming ___ an adult is with you.
hints: The sentence gives a condition for going swimming.
You need a conjunction that means except if or not before.
Read the sentence with your word. Does it keep children safe?
items.explanation: Unless means except if, so you can only swim when an adult is with you. Until would also work.

items.prompt: Where does the comma go? Although the test was hard Rani finished it on time.

options.why: Although starts the clause, so it should not be cut off from the rest of it.
Was hard belongs with the test, so the clause has not finished.
Rani is the start of the main clause and belongs with finished.

hints: The sentence begins with a subordinate clause.
Put the comma where the subordinate clause ends and the main clause begins.
Find the main clause first. Who finished the test on time?
items.explanation: The subordinate clause Although the test was hard comes first, so a comma separates it from the main clause.

items.prompt: Join the two sentences into one using although. The film was long. We enjoyed every minute.

answers: Although the film was long, we enjoyed every minute
We enjoyed every minute although the film was long
We enjoyed every minute, although the film was long

hints: Although shows a contrast between the two ideas.
You can put the although clause first or second. If it comes first, add a comma after it.
Decide which idea goes in the although clause. Which idea makes the other one surprising?
items.explanation: Although the film was long, we enjoyed every minute. The although clause can also come second: We enjoyed every minute although the film was long.

items.prompt: Choose all the sentences where the subordinate clause comes first.

options.text: Before the match started, the players shook hands.
Mum smiled when she saw the cake.
options.why: The subordinate clause when she saw the cake comes second.

options.text: If you finish early, you can read a book.
We ran inside because it started to rain.
options.why: The subordinate clause because it started to rain comes second.

options.text: As soon as the bell rang, everyone stood up.

hints: Find the subordinate clause in each sentence first.
When a subordinate clause comes first, it is usually followed by a comma.
Look at the first word of each sentence. Is it a conjunction?
items.explanation: Before the match started, If you finish early and As soon as the bell rang are subordinate clauses at the start, followed by commas.

items.prompt: Which sentence has two subordinate clauses?

options.text: We arrived at the museum and it was closed.
options.why: This joins two main clauses with and.

options.text: The museum, which is new, was closed.
options.why: This has only one subordinate clause: which is new.

options.text: The museum was closed on Monday.
options.why: This is a simple sentence.

options.text: When we arrived, the museum was closed because it was a holiday.

hints: Count the clauses in each sentence carefully.
Look for conjunctions and relative pronouns that start subordinate clauses.
Look for one sentence with a clause that starts with when and a clause that starts with because.
items.explanation: When we arrived and because it was a holiday are both subordinate clauses. The museum was closed is the main clause.

items.prompt: Maya took an umbrella ___ it was raining.
hints: The second part gives a reason.
Which word joins a reason to the main idea?
Try each word and see which one makes sense.
items.explanation: Because introduces the reason. It makes the second part a subordinate clause.

items.prompt: Which part is the subordinate clause? We will go to the park if the rain stops.

options.text: We will go to the park
options.why: This part can stand alone, so it is the main clause.
This is only a phrase. It has no verb.
This is only a verb. It is not a whole clause.

hints: A subordinate clause cannot stand alone as a sentence.
Look for the conjunction if.
Which part starts with a word that makes you ask what happens next?
items.explanation: If the rain stops needs the main clause to make sense, so it is the subordinate clause.

items.prompt: Build the complex sentence.
items.answer: Although she was tired, Putri finished her homework.
hints: The sentence starts with a conjunction.
The comma comes after the subordinate clause.
Finish with her homework.
items.explanation: Although she was tired is the subordinate clause. A comma follows it, then the main clause.

items.prompt: Sort the joining words.
hints: Words like and and but join clauses of equal importance.
Words that start a clause that cannot stand alone are subordinating.
Think about whether the clause after the word can stand alone.
items.explanation: And, but, so and or join main clauses. Because, although, while and unless begin subordinate clauses.

items.prompt: Match each conjunction to its job.
hints: Think of a sentence with each word.
Although means in spite of.
Unless means if not.
items.explanation: Because gives a reason, although shows contrast, unless means if not, and until shows an end point in time.

items.prompt: Put the parts in order to make a complex sentence.
hints: The first card begins with a capital letter.
Unless starts the subordinate clause.
The main clause follows the comma.
items.explanation: Unless you hurry is the subordinate clause, then the main clause tells what happens.

items.prompt: Choose the conjunction that fits. You will not pass the test ___ you practise.

options.why: Because gives a reason, but here we need a condition.
While means at the same time.
Although shows a contrast and does not fit the meaning.

hints: The sentence says what must happen to pass.
It needs a word that means if not.
Replace the gap with if not and see if the meaning matches.
items.explanation: Unless means if not. You will not pass if you do not practise.

items.prompt: Complete the table.
head: Sentence
Main clause
Subordinate clause
hints: The main clause can stand alone.
Here, the subordinate clause starts with a conjunction.
Row 2: take the part after the comma.
items.explanation: The main clause makes sense alone. Here, the subordinate clause begins with a conjunction.

items.prompt: Write one conjunction that shows how long. Tom kept reading ___ his mother called him for dinner.
hints: Think about when Tom stopped reading.
The word shows an end point.
The conjunction means up to the time that.
items.explanation: Until shows the time when Tom stopped reading.

items.prompt: ___ Hadi was hungry, he waited ___ his friends arrived.
hints: Read the whole sentence before choosing.
The first gap shows a contrast with waiting.
Hungry people usually eat, but Hadi waited, so the first word shows a surprising contrast.
items.explanation: Although shows contrast. Until shows how long he waited.

items.prompt: Choose 2 complex sentences.

options.why: This joins two main clauses with and, so it is a compound sentence.

options.text: Because the road was flooded, we took the train.
Amara waited while her brother bought tickets.
The cat sat on the mat.
options.why: This has one clause, so it is a simple sentence.

options.text: I like tea, but my sister likes juice.
options.why: This joins two main clauses with but, so it is a compound sentence.

hints: A complex sentence has a main clause and a subordinate clause.
Look for because or while.
Cross out sentences joined by and or but.
items.explanation: Because and while start subordinate clauses. Here, and and but join main clauses.

items.prompt: Which sentence is NOT a complex sentence?

options.text: Although I was tired, I kept walking.
options.why: This has a subordinate clause with although.

options.text: I kept walking because I wanted to see the sunrise.
options.why: This has a subordinate clause with because.

options.text: I was tired but I kept walking.
When the hill got steeper, I kept walking.
options.why: This has a subordinate clause with when.

hints: Look for a clause that cannot stand alone.
But joins two equal clauses.
Check which sentence has no subordinating conjunction.
items.explanation: But joins two main clauses, so it is a compound sentence. The others each have a subordinate clause.

items.prompt: Which one is a sentence fragment?

options.text: Although it was late, Rangga kept working.
options.why: This has both a subordinate clause and a main clause.

options.text: The electricity went out, so we lit candles.
options.why: This has two complete clauses joined by so.

options.text: We lit candles because the electricity went out.
options.why: This has a main clause first, then a subordinate clause.

hints: A full sentence needs a main clause.
Which one stops without telling us what happened?
Look for a sentence that is only a subordinate clause.
items.explanation: Because the electricity went out leaves us waiting for the main clause, so it is a fragment.

items.prompt: Which sentence joins the ideas best? It was raining. We still went to the market. We needed bread.

options.text: Although it was raining we needed bread, we went to the market.
options.why: The clauses are mixed up and the meaning is unclear.

options.text: It was raining, because we went to the market, we needed bread.
options.why: Because does not fit here. The rain was not caused by going to the market.

options.text: We went to the market although we needed bread because it was raining.
options.why: This says the rain was the reason we needed bread, which changes the meaning.

options.text: Although it was raining, we went to the market because we needed bread.

hints: Check what each sentence says caused what.
Rain did not cause the need for bread.
Find the sentence where although shows contrast and because gives the reason for going.
items.explanation: It shows contrast with although and gives the real reason with because.

items.prompt: True or false: In the sentence "Since it was late, we went home", since means because.
hints: Replace since with because.
Does it still make sense?
Yes.
items.explanation: Since can give a reason. It was late is the reason they went home.

items.prompt: True or false: The word unless means if not.
hints: Replace unless with if not.
Try it in a sentence.
It sets a condition.
items.explanation: We can go out unless it rains means we can go out if it does not rain.

items.prompt: True or false: The words "Although she was tired" make a complete sentence on their own.
hints: Does it feel finished?
It leaves us waiting for more.
It needs a main clause.
items.explanation: Although she was tired is a subordinate clause. It needs a main clause such as she kept running.

items.prompt: True or false: A subordinate clause cannot stand alone as a sentence.
hints: Can it be a sentence by itself?
It often starts with a conjunction.
It depends on another clause.
items.explanation: A subordinate clause depends on a main clause to make sense. For example, because I was hungry needs I ate lunch.

items.prompt: True or false: In the sentence "Because I was hungry, I ate lunch", the main clause is "Because I was hungry".
hints: Which part can stand alone?
The conjunction starts the other clause.
Main clauses can be sentences.
items.explanation: The main clause is I ate lunch because it can stand alone. Because I was hungry is the subordinate clause.

items.prompt: True or false: In the sentence "I will help you if you ask", the main clause is "I will help you".
hints: Which part can stand alone?
Remove the part beginning with if.
The main clause is the first part.
items.explanation: I will help you makes sense alone. If you ask is the subordinate clause.

items.prompt: ___ it was cold, we went swimming.
hints: The ideas contrast.
We expect not to swim.
Although shows contrast.
items.explanation: Although shows that the two ideas are surprising together.
